On 17 August 2010 at 13:22, Roger Bivand wrote:

Yup, thanks for posting the reminder.

Indeed -- it all went pretty smoothly.

The one sour note (particularly for me as mentor) is that Yasuhisa ceased all
communications related to the project in June and hence failed the mid-term.
Even pinging by two friends in Japan didn't help :-/

Apparently the "loss rate" is about 10% at GSoC so R is still under par over
the first four years even with our first fail.

Cheers, Dirk

On 17 August 2010 at 10:32, Ian Fellows wrote:
| Do we have to submit code somewhere?

I believe this to be a 'can' and not a 'must' -- the 'timeline' in the GSoC
2010 FAQ lists 'August 30: Students can begin submitting code sample to
Google'.

I don't think you have too, and as I recall, in the past we simply pointed to
a (public) code repository (such as Google Code to R-Forge).

If anybody has firmer details, please share.

Dirk

--

I got a mail from the GSoC team regarding the mode of submission [0]. However, I don't know if the mentors did get it or can access this particular link. In any case, I am including the details here:

Monday, 30 August 2010:

All projects for all organizations with passing students will be created on Project Hosting on Google Code <http://code.google.com/hosting/>.  Student can begin uploading their code samples.

Friday, 10 September 2010: 19:00 UTC (12:00 noon Pacific Time)

"Soft" deadline for student code sample submission. What this means: if you get us your code sample by this "soft deadline," you will be in the first round of t-shirts to be shipped. Otherwise you'll need to wait until we have time to do one offs.

Regards,
Chillu

[0] http://groups.google.com/group/google-summer-of-code-students-list/web/code-submission-guidelines-2010?pli=1

messages.subject: Re: Final Evaluation
messages.body_plain:
Actually, code submission is a requirement this year (see http://groups.google.com/group/google-summer-of-code-students-list/web/code-submission-guidelines-2010):

As a *requirement* for the Google Summer of CodeTM, all students who receive passing final evaluations will need to provide a copy of the code they produced as part of participating in the program.  [...]  We will begin sending final program payments to all students whether or not we have a code sample on file for you, but we will send neither t-shirt nor certificate to you until we have received your code sample.

*Any student who does not provide a code sample will be expected to return the final program payment to us.*

Best,
Felix

messages.subject: Final-ish Blog posts?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I was wondering if I could get our four successful students to write up a
(short !!) note for the blog about the GSoC experience: what worked, what
didn't, what you liked, what you hated -- any form or topic works.

It is useful to mark some of those thoughts now and it should help us and
others for 2011 and beyond.  Can I count on you to do something -- anything,
really -- say between now and Sunday?  I am sure we can count on blogmaster
Tal to hep with "production" issues.

Blog posts by mentors or casual observers would also be an options -- whoever
wants to should be welcome.

Cheers, Dirk

--
Dirk Eddelbuettel | e...@debian.org | http://dirk.eddelbuettel.com
